title: Brief SIRS with no organ dysfunction: weak sepsis evidence
discharge_summary: SYNTHETIC CASE - NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient: Synthetic Patient 08, 58-year-old female. MRN: SYN-0008
Reason for admission: Burning with urination, urinary frequency, and fever.

On arrival her temperature was 38.4 C and heart rate 104. Both normalized within 6 hours after acetaminophen and oral fluids. Blood pressure was 128/76 and remained normal. White blood cell count was 11.2. Lactate was 1.4. Creatinine, bilirubin, and platelet count were normal, and mental status was normal throughout. Urine culture grew E. coli. She was treated with IV ceftriaxone for 24 hours and then oral cephalexin.
1. Acute cystitis due to E. coli
Discharge plan: Cephalexin to complete 5 days. Follow up with primary care as needed.

expected.notes: Fever and tachycardia briefly, normal lactate, and no organ dysfunction. These are not enough clinical indicators to query for sepsis; a sepsis query here would be unsupported. No candidates.
